tools.name: resolve
tools.description: Which model to call for a need, on the providers the user has accounts with: the provider's own model id, its price, capabilities and the reason. Give `providers` and a `task` or a `purpose`; add `needs`, `budget`, `origin` and other constraints to narrow it. `shape` asks for a team or an escalation

tools.name: plan
tools.description: Reads a description of the work (a prompt, tags, attachment types and sizes) into a need, then resolves it as `resolve` does. Use `resolve` when you can state the task or purpose yourself; use this when you only have the user's words. Counts as more than one call. The answer depends on these goals;

tools.name: stack
tools.description: For an agent that has to work with named systems (Linear, GitHub, Postgres…): what to connect for each, and which model to call. Give `systems`, `target` (local or cloud) and the `harness` the agent runs in; add `model.providers` to get a model too. Each system's choice is its owner's own MCP server

tools.name: platform
tools.description: Where an app's agent runs: give `requires` (baa, gpu, private_network, edge, long_running, websockets, scheduled_jobs, large_uploads) with `longest_turn_seconds` and `largest_upload_mb` where they apply, and the goals you have. tools.name: list_models
tools.description: The catalog's models with each provider's offering, price, capabilities and quality scores, filtered by task, providers and needs. tools.name: get_model
tools.description: One model by id (`vendor/model`, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`): every provider's offering with its price history, capabilities, limits and dates, and the model's quality scores. Counts as one call.

tools.name: list_purposes
tools.description: The purpose presets `resolve` accepts: named jobs such as reading receipts or a coding agent, each with the task, needs and budget it stands for. Free.

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description: The goals an answer depends on (cost, depth, where a model's maker is based, where data may stay, languages, the kind of data, the accounts already held), each with one question to ask the user, the options to offer and the parameters each answer is sent as, and the rules for asking. tools.name: get_vocabulary
tools.description: Every name the other tools accept: tasks, capabilities and their levels, providers, origin groups, budgets and team strategies. Free.
